Is it Just the Power of Control?

It isn't inherent, that's for sure. Some smaller and less "political" subs actually have rather nice moderator staffs that do their jobs effectively.

You know what I think it is?

I think it's that the mods are handed the reigns of a sub and they suddenly realize that their opinions matter more than anyone else's.

And once you've fully convinced yourself that you're more important than everyone else, well you won't take too kindly to anyone who challenges this view. People who disagree with you must be wrong, right? After all, they put YOU in charge, not him.

And once you start rationalizing THAT, you're just one step away from deleting the accounts of everyone who challenges your divine grace. Because it's the logical next step - after all, we want GOOD content on our subreddit, so why should we let people who are so obviously wrong pollute our precious new queue? They deserve to be deleted really, they should have realized how wrong they were.

At least that's how I see it as. You and I can't look at a moderator a month after he was appointed and see exactly what led to him being a meglomaniac, but I have a feeling it's just a series of logical progressions like that.

When I was very little I read books for leisure but not super insane amounts of books.

The Golden Compass by Phillip Pullman changed that when i was like, 7. Made me into a very voracious reader over time. I would read at least 2 books a week.

I ended up just constantly having my nose in a book once I was 11 because I developed chronic insomnia. My dad claimed that I wasn't sleeping because I was reading, but it was the other way around. I still have chronic insomnia as well, and I don't recommend it.

I would end up reading several books at a time and would finish at least one of those books a day, only to have it replaced by another book. My dad would brag to his friends and then get mad at me at home because I hadn't done the dishes yet, or I needed to vaccuum, or I had a poor grade on a math quiz, even though that was because the teacher wouldn't teach me properly because she thought I was just like my sister who had liked to pass nasty notes about her. So I read in math class because she wouldn't help me. She also had problems with my friend who has a math learning disability. That teacher almost got fired because of the bs she put us through. Two out of three strikes.

My english teacher, while amazed and encouraging of my reading, would get annoyed when I read too far ahead in book assignments, but I wouldn't even realise that I was so far ahead. What took most kids 20 minutes to read took me 5. So my teacher would put a sticky note at each chapter and then take away my book once I hit the sticky note or, more usually, passed it because I was just so in to reading.

And honestly, I likely wouldn't have become such a huge reader if not for The Golden Compass, which I chose to read because I had to stay home on a rainy day. I do read less for leisure now, but I am in college and have work.

But wheneverthe good old chronic insomnia starts to hit hard again, I usually pass the time with reading. After a certain point it gets hard to be productive and work on school stuff with the time of should-be-sleeping, but reading I am always able to do.
